record.file_problem: Repository metadata, README, and file list only; code and experiment outputs were not read or run.
record.tranche_reason: The README reports behavioral results from adding category-specific, difference-in-means steering vectors and a learned low-rank intervention. These interventions test refusal control with a different recipe from the original single-direction, all-layer ablation.
record.gate_note: The README reports benchmark results and direction-comparison results. Setup commands and the listed scripts are not evidence that code was run by this reader. The reported standard errors are said to be available in the paper and project page, but are not provided in this README.
record.test_reason: The study builds difference-in-means refusal directions (one per refusal category) at layer 18 and steers with them. Refusal on harmful prompts rises, benign over-refusal falls, and capability is checked. It also transfers a learned combination of these directions to two same-architecture variants and compares the directions with the base model's. The recipe differs from the original: category-specific and top-K sparsified vectors, one layer, the sign set by a probe, and no ablation.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The record omits one stated conclusion: refusal-token fine-tuning creates the category directions rather than inheriting them from the base model. The authors infer this from near-orthogonal base-model vectors and sharper clustering. They call transfer useful but not perfectly model-invariant.
record.recipe_differences: Research/tool repository with reported results. It uses category-specific differences between refusal-token and benign activations, top-200 feature selection, layer-18 steering, and a learned low-rank combination; it does not reproduce the original single direction with all-layer projection ablation.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported outcome varies by benchmark, including XSTest Safe and Do-Not-Answer for transferred Llama 3 8B Instruct; effects also differ between categorical steering and the low-rank combination.

fits_no_version.finding: Refusal-token fine-tuning yields separable category-aligned directions, one per CoCoNot refusal type, and each can be steered separately.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Refusal reasons (safety, humanizing, incomplete, unsupported, indeterminate) occupy distinct steerable directions in models trained with categorical refusal tokens.

record.peer_reviewed: 2025 NeurIPS Mechanistic Interpretability Workshop; 2026 COLM Actionable Interpretability Workshop (as stated in README)
record.problems: This is a README-level record: code was not read or run. Standard errors are referenced but not included in the README. The reported intervention is layer-specific and differs from the original ablation.
record.rows_left_out: The README gives individual benign- and harmful-benchmark cells and individual general-capability benchmark scores. These were not separately extracted because the aggregate results and outcome-changing cells were prioritized; see README Results tables. The listed files and scripts were not treated as executed results.

untested.parts: Directional ablation or projection-out at all layers. A single global direction. Unconditional addition inducing refusal on harmless prompts.
Jailbreaks suppressing the direction; adversarial training against ablation.
No comparison of single versus multi-direction, cone or affine descriptions. No inter-category cosine similarities reported.
Harmfulness encoded separately from the refusal decision. A harmfulness probe is used but not analysed for this.
Cross-language transfer. Transfer of the raw difference-in-means direction, as opposed to the trained low-rank vector. Other architectures.
Variation of training data, timing or method beyond the base versus refusal-token fine-tuned comparison.
DeepSeek R1 Distill receives only a transferred vector. Its own direction and the effect of reasoning before answering are not studied.

missing.what: Logit bias toward [respond] fails while residual steering succeeds. This is a qualitative single example, not a rate.
missing.locator: README 'Why Not Just Force the Respond Token?'

missing.what: Standard errors and the full paper's analyses. The paper (arXiv 2603.13359) was not read, only the README.

record.verdict_notes: Verdicts rest on the README only. The recipe departs from the original in several ways: category-specific, top-200 sparsified vectors at layer 18; the sign is chosen by a probe; the transferred vector is trained, not raw difference-in-means. Treat V1 support as steering-based, not ablation-based. DeepSeek R1 Distill is a reasoning model, but the study does not examine reasoning, so V8 is left untested.

versions.untested_parts: No ablation or projection-out experiment; no all-layer/all-position intervention; no test of a single global direction. Steering is at layer 18, uses category-specific vectors or a low-rank combination, and is signed according to a probe.
No jailbreak suppression of the direction or training against its ablation.
The README reports category-specific directions and steering outcomes, but does not compare affine, cone, and dominant-direction geometries directly.
No result separates a harmfulness judgment from the refusal decision.
Tests transfer of the learned low-rank vector to two same-architecture model variants. No language transfer, base-to-instruct transfer of the original direction, or other architecture is reported.
Compares Llama 3 8B Base with refusal-token fine-tuned Refuse-Llama; does not vary training data, timing, or training procedure.
Although DeepSeek R1 Distill Llama is listed as a transfer target, the README does not test whether reasoning before answering changes the direction or its effects.
